div.head: Hn Lond 15
div.ab: Et ciues habeant fugationes suas ad fugandum, sicut melius et plenius habuerunt antecessores eorum, scilicet in Chiltre et Middelsexe et Sureie.
Et cives habeant fugationes suas ad fugandum sicut melius et plenius habuerunt antecessores eorum, scilicet [Ch]iltre e Middelsexe e Sureie.
And the citizens shall enjoy as good and full hunting-rights as their ancestors ever did, namely, in the Chilterns, Middlesex and Surrey.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 292–293 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 526, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

Vgl. Gl Jagd Z. 3. 10 n. 7; Forst 20; London 22. [fugare in der anderen Bed. ‘(Weidevieh) auftreiben’ auch Durham Halmote books p. 11a. 1296.] Jagd wird im 12. Jh. auch anderen Städten verbrieft, bisweilen nur niedere (Ballard 83); Stubbs Lect. 128 erblickt auch hierin nur diese. Round sieht (Athenæ. 30 June 1894, 838) hierin ein Zeichen, dass Londons Jagdrecht beschränkt worden war. Erweislich verbot Wilhelm I. den Londonern nur venationem in cervos, cervas, capreolas [also Hochjagd] auf Lanfrancs Landgut Harrow, ausser wem der sie erlaube; Davis Reg. Agn. n. 265.—Im Freibriefe 1155 wird Londons Jagd-Privileg wiederholt, aber kein Ortsname genannt.—Essex fehlt unter den Jagdgründen der Londoner, weil es Königsforst war

Cf. Gl Jagd ll. 3. 10 n. 7; Forst 20; London 22. [fugare in the other meaning ‘to drive (grazing cattle) out to pasture’ also in Durham Halmote books p. 11a. 1296.] In the 12th cent. hunting rights are granted by charter to other towns too, sometimes only the lesser hunting (Ballard 83); Stubbs Lect. 128 sees only this here too. Round (Athenæ. 30 June 1894, 838) sees in this a sign that London’s hunting right had been restricted. What can be proved is that William I forbade the Londoners only venationem in cervos, cervas, capreolas [thus the greater hunting] on Lanfranc’s estate of Harrow, except for anyone to whom he gave leave; Davis Reg. Agn. n. 265.—In the charter of 1155 London’s hunting privilege is repeated, but no place-name is given.—Essex is missing from the Londoners’ hunting grounds because it was royal forest

Chiltern, Hügel in Oxfordshire, Bucks., Herts. bei St. Albans und Wendover, einst dicht bewaldet, waren durch Wulfhere von Mercien im 7. Jh. Wessex entrissen. (De desertis Ciltine et Ondred [Andredesweald] kam 686 Ceadwalla von Wessex; Stephan V. Wilfr. 42.) Schon hieraus folgt, dass dies Jagdrecht nicht aus einer Gebietshoheit Londons zur Römerzeit mit Gomme Making of London 70 hergeleitet werden darf

The Chilterns, hills in Oxfordshire, Bucks. and Herts. near St Albans and Wendover, once densely wooded, had been wrested from Wessex by Wulfhere of Mercia in the 7th cent. (Ceadwalla of Wessex came De desertis Ciltine et Ondred [Andredesweald] in 686; Stephan V. Wilfr. 42.) This alone shows that this hunting right may not be derived, with Gomme Making of London 70, from a territorial sovereignty of London in Roman times
